criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
cp local-to-S3 followed by cp S3-to-local produces a local file byte-identical to the original local source file (round-trip invariant verified in trajectory).
cp with two s3:// URIs (S3-to-S3 copy) results in both the source and destination objects existing afterward, verified via ls or get.
When cp is invoked with --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <key>, the stored object's metadata/head-object output reflects server-side KMS encryption referencing that key.
ls with no path lists all owned buckets with creation dates, and ls with --recursive on a prefix produces a flat listing with no 'PRE' directory entries.
ls against a non-existent bucket, a prefix matching no keys, or an unknown flag like --extra-argument-foo exits non-zero with stderr populated and stdout empty, not a raw traceback.

mv with source equal to destination S3 URI fails with non-zero exit and an error naming the self-move class (e.g. 'Cannot mv a file onto itself'); a bare 'mv' with missing arguments also fails non-zero.
criteria.contract_ref: s3 mv: same-URI and missing-argument behavior

criteria.text: After a successful mv (local-to-S3, S3-to-S3, or S3-to-local), the source (local file or S3 key) no longer exists and the destination exists, consistent with cp-then-remove-source semantics.

rb on a non-empty bucket without --force fails with non-zero exit and does not delete the bucket or its objects; rb with --force removes all objects then the bucket, after which the bucket no longer appears in bucket listing.
criteria.contract_ref: s3 rb: non-empty bucket and --force behavior

criteria.text: rb on a non-existent bucket exits non-zero with a stderr message and empty stdout.
A second sync run over an unchanged source/destination pair transfers nothing (no new operation lines beyond prior state); sync from a non-existent local source directory fails with non-zero exit.
criteria.contract_ref: s3 sync: idempotency and non-existent source

criteria.text: After sync, the destination's object/file set is a superset of the source's, and objects/files present only at the destination are NOT removed unless --delete is passed.
criteria.contract_ref: s3 sync: superset invariant and default no-delete

criteria.text: On every success case exercised, stdout contains only progress/operation lines and stderr is empty; on every failure case exercised, stdout is empty and stderr contains a human-readable error naming the failure class (never a raw stack trace), with exit code in {1,2,252,255}.
criteria.contract_ref: Output contract: stdout/stderr and exit codes
